# Data Assembly Process of VegVault 2.0.0

```{r}
#| label: source config
#| include: FALSE
#| results: 'hide'
#| warning: FALSE
#| message: FALSE

library(here)

here::i_am("website/database_assembly.qmd")

# Load configuration
source(
  here::here(
    "R/00_Config_file.R"
  )
)
```

[VegVault]{.vegvault} v2.0.0 has been assembled through systematic integration of multiple publicly available databases, each contributing specialized data types to create a comprehensive vegetation database spanning both temporal and ecological dimensions.
Each data source is processed in its own repository and released with a tag, and the database is built from these tagged files only.

The assembly workflow visualization:

```{r}
#| label: assembly scheme
#| echo: false
knitr::include_graphics(
  here::here(
    "Outputs/Figures/DB_assembly_visualisation/assembly_workflow.png"
  )
)

```

## Figure legend:

**Primary data sources**:

1. **[Neotoma Paleoecology Database](https://www.neotomadb.org/)** - [Fossil pollen data]{.paleo} (0-20,000 years BP)
2. **[sPlotOpen](https://idiv-biodiversity.de/en/splot/splotopen.html)** - [Contemporary vegetation plots]{.neo-vegetation}
3. **[BIEN](https://bien.nceas.ucsb.edu/bien/)** - [Contemporary vegetation]{.neo-vegetation} and [functional traits]{.traits}
4. **[TRY Plant Trait Database](https://www.try-db.org/TryWeb/Home.php)** - Comprehensive [plant functional traits]{.traits}
5. **[CHELSA](https://chelsa-climate.org/)** - High-resolution [climate data]{.abiotic} (contemporary and paleoclimate)
6. **[Harmonized World Soil Database (HWSD) v2.2](https://data.apps.fao.org/catalog/iso/ff5c613c-75bb-46a9-a162-bc728059b465)** - Global [soil data]{.abiotic} (VegVault 1.0.0 named this source WoSIS)

**Data Processing**: Individual processing pipelines for each data type using specialized [GitHub repositories]{.reproducibility}

7. **[VegVault-FOSSILPOL v2.0.0](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-FOSSILPOL/tree/v2.0.0)** - [Fossil pollen data]{.paleo} processing
8. **[VegVault-Vegetation_data v2.0.0](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-Vegetation_data/tree/v2.0.0)** - [Contemporary vegetation]{.neo-vegetation} processing
9. **[VegVault-Trait_data v2.0.0](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-Trait_data/tree/v2.0.0)** - [Functional trait data]{.traits} processing
10. **[VegVault-abiotic_data v2.0.0](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-abiotic_data/tree/v2.0.0)** - [Environmental data]{.abiotic} processing
11. **[VegVault v2.0.0](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/tree/v2.0.0)** - Consolidation into unified [SQLite database]{.database} structure with key steps:
    - **[Taxonomic Harmonization]{.taxa}**: Using the {taxospace} R package to align taxa with GBIF backbone
    - **[Trait Categorization]{.traits}**: Grouping [traits]{.traits} into functional domains following [Díaz et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature16489)
    - **Spatial-Temporal Linking**: Creating gridpoints for [abiotic data]{.abiotic} and linking to [vegetation samples]{.neo-vegetation}
12. **[VegVault]{.vegvault} database** - The released [SQLite database]{.database} (see [Database Access](database_access.qmd))

## Reproducibility Through Version Control {.topic-reproducibility .topic-icon}

All [VegVault]{.vegvault} processing repositories use [GitHub Tags](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/viewing-your-repositorys-releases-and-tags) to ensure complete [reproducibility]{.reproducibility}.
For v2.0.0, every input file of the build is pinned by repository, tag, file name and SHA-256 checksum in [`Data/Producers/producer_manifest.yml`](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/blob/v2.0.0/Data/Producers/producer_manifest.yml), checked against its data specification before the build, and listed with its tag in the table `BuildProducers` of the database.
The table `version_control` of the database records the build profile, the git commit of the code and the checksum of the pin manifest, enabling exact replication of the [database assembly]{.database} process.

## Data Processing Details

### Fossil Pollen Records {.topic-paleo .topic-icon}

[Fossil pollen records]{.paleo} have been downloaded from the [Neotoma Paleoecology Database](https://www.neotomadb.org/) using their API on 19th November 2026 (VegVault 1.0.0 used the download of 26th June 2023).
All data acquisition and processing have been done using the [FOSSILPOL: Workflow for processing and standardizing global paleoecological pollen data](https://bit.ly/FOSSILPOL) (version 1.0.0), with the settings of VegVault 1.0.0.
This includes the selection of depositional environments, ecological groups, chronology control point types, and a minimum number of chronology control points to construct age-depth models.
Individual samples and records have been filtered by age limits, number of [pollen grains]{.paleo}, maximum age interpolation, and number of valid levels.
In addition, the accuracy of [fossil pollen data]{.paleo} is increased by re-estimating all age-depth models using the Bayesian probabilistic approach and including the information about individual age uncertainty.
Age-depth models of VegVault 1.0.0 are reused for records whose chronology did not change since the 2023 download, and fitted again for the others.

**Selection Criteria:**

- Only records with type "pollen" with valid geological coordinates (longitude between -180 and 180, latitude between -90 and 90)
- Depositional environments: lakes, bogs, and mires only ([selection table](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-FOSSILPOL/blob/v2.0.0/Data/Input/Depositional_environment/Neotoma/depositional_environment_selection_2026-11-19.csv))
- Specific ecological groups retained ([selection tables](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-FOSSILPOL/tree/v2.0.0/Data/Input/Eco_group))
- Minimum 5 chronology control points ([valid types](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault-FOSSILPOL/blob/v2.0.0/Data/Input/Chronology_setting/Chron_control_point_types/chron_control_point_types_2026-11-19.csv))

**Quality Filters:**

- Minimum 125 [pollen grains]{.paleo} per sample (balanced for data retention vs. quality)
  - While the preferred minimum was initially set at 150, this threshold resulted in significant data loss
  - Threshold adjusted to 125 with condition that less than 75% of samples would have low pollen sum
- Age limits: 0-20,000 cal yr BP
- Exclusion of samples older than 3000 years of the last chronology control point
- Minimum 5 samples per record
- Re-calculated age-depth models using Bayesian approach [{Bchron} package](https://andrewcparnell.github.io/Bchron/)

**Processing Details**: Available at [VegVault-FOSSILPOL](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24505587)

### Contemporary Vegetation Plots {.topic-neo-vegetation .topic-icon}

The primary sources of [contemporary plot-based vegetation data]{.neo-vegetation} are BIEN (Botanical Information and Ecology Network) and sPlotOpen (the open-access version of sPlot).

**BIEN Processing:**

- Downloaded using [{BIEN} R package](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/BIEN/index.html) v1.2.8 on 20th November 2026 from BIEN database 4.2.8, the database version of VegVault 1.0.0, using function `BIEN::BIEN_plot_datasource()`
- Retained key columns: `datasource_id`, `datasource`, `plot_name`, `sampling_protocol`, `methodology_reference`, `methodology_description`, `longitude`, `latitude`, `plot_area_ha`, `subplot`, `individual_count`, `family_matched`, `name_matched`, `name_matched_author`, `verbatim_family`, `verbatim_scientific_name`, `scrubbed_species_binomial`, `scrubbed_taxonomic_status`, `scrubbed_family`, `scrubbed_author`
- All columns renamed using [snake case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_case)
- Filtered out records with missing essential information (NA values in `datasource_id`, `datasource`, `plot_name`, `longitude`, `latitude`, and/or `plot_area_ha`)
- Records of one taxon (`name_matched`) in a plot merged into one record, with their individual counts added
- Only the latest survey kept for plots surveyed more than once
- One row per plot, with a stable plot identifier `plot_id`

**sPlotOpen Processing:**

- sPlotOpen v2.0, downloaded on 26th September 2023 for VegVault 1.0.0 and kept, as no newer open release exists
- Linked tables `DT2.oa` and `header.oa` via `PlotObservationID` column
- Applied quality filters for geographic and area data (filtered out rows with NA values in `PlotObservationID`, `GIVD_ID`, `Longitude`, `Latitude`, and/or `Releve_area`)
- Records without a species name dropped, and records of one species in a plot merged into one record
- All columns renamed using [snake case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_case)

**Processing Details**: Available at [VegVault-Vegetation_data](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24505586)

### Functional Traits {.topic-traits .topic-icon}

Following [Díaz et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature16489), we selected six key [functional traits]{.traits} representing:

- `Stem specific density`
- `Leaf nitrogen content per unit mass`
- `Diaspore mass`
- `Plant height`
- `Leaf area`
- `Leaf mass per area`

**[TRY Database]{.traits} Processing:**

- Data request ID: `28498` on 29th August 2023, the request of VegVault 1.0.0 (no new request was made)
- Requested [traits]{.traits} with codes: `3106`, `4`, `3108`, `3110`, `3112`, `3114`, `3116`, `3117`, `14`, and `26` (closest to Díaz et al. 2016 description)
- The request file is read with the same settings as `rtry::rtry_import()`
- For each [trait]{.traits} (`TraitID`), extracted all relevant observations (`ObservationID`), ensuring only observations unique to each [trait]{.traits}
- Identified all unique data (`DataID`) associated with each [trait]{.traits}
- Excluded non-meaningful [trait]{.traits} variations (DataID: `2221`, `2222`, `2223`, `2224`, `2225`, `3646`, `3647`, `3698`, `3699`, `3727`, `3728`, `3730`, `3731`, `3849`, `3850`, `4029`, and `4030`), e.g., `height at 15 days`
- Extracted covariate information (additional data stored in `DataName` column)
- Trait values taken from TRY's standardised values (`StdValue`)
- Removed records that TRY flags as copies of another record, and repeated values of one [trait]{.traits} within one observation
- Impossible, unparsable or incomplete coordinates set to missing
- All columns renamed using [snake case](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_case)
- Added `Trait Domain` variable to group [traits]{.traits} following Díaz et al. (2016) selection for efficient extraction across TRY and BIEN

**[BIEN Traits]{.traits} Processing:**

- Downloaded using {BIEN} R package v1.2.8 on 19th November 2026 from BIEN database 4.2.8, using function `BIEN::BIEN_trait_trait()`
- Requested [traits]{.traits}: `whole plant height`, `stem wood density`, `leaf area`, `leaf area per leaf dry mass`, `leaf nitrogen content per leaf dry mass`, and `seed mass`
- Retained columns: `trait_name`, `trait_value`, `unit`, `id`, `longitude`, `latitude`, `method`, `url_source`, `source_citation`, `project_pi`, `scrubbed_species_binomial`, and `access`
- Removed records from sources that copy a compilation held by TRY and match a published TRY record (the TRY copy is kept)

**Units and quality checks (both providers):**

- Every value converted to the single unit of its trait domain by a registered and versioned rule; values whose unit is not registered, or whose conversion fails, are not published
- `leaf mass per area` derived from specific leaf area (`leaf area per leaf dry mass`) as 1/value, after the specific leaf area is converted to a known unit
- Values from sources whose scale is physically implausible not published

**Processing Details**: Available at [VegVault-Trait_data](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24505585)

### Abiotic Environmental Data {.topic-abiotic .topic-icon}

The primary sources of [abiotic data]{.abiotic} are CHELSA, CHELSA-TRACE21, and the Harmonized World Soil Database (HWSD) v2.2.
The first two data sources provide high-resolution downscaled [climatic data]{.abiotic}, while the latter offers detailed [soil information]{.abiotic} (only available for [contemporary data]{.neo-vegetation}).
VegVault 1.0.0 used HWSD v2.0 or v2.01 (the exact version was not recorded) and named it WoSIS or SoilGrids.

**[CHELSA Climate Data]{.abiotic}:**

- [Contemporary]{.neo-vegetation}: CHELSA v2.1, all seven files downloaded on 20th November 2026 (VegVault 1.0.0: 8th September 2023)
- Used [{ClimDatDownloadR} R package](https://github.com/HelgeJentsch/ClimDatDownloadR) with function `ClimDatDownloadR::Chelsa.Clim.download()`
- Selected bio-variables: `1`, `4`, `6`, `12`, `15`, `18`, `19`
- Spatial aggregation: 25x factor using median values with [{terra} R package](https://rspatial.github.io/terra/) function `terra::aggregate(factor = 25, fun = "median")`
- `bio4` (temperature seasonality) in hundredths of a degree Celsius; in VegVault 1.0.0 it was 0 south of about 65.7° N because of a truncated download
- A `bio12` value of 6553.5 is the storage limit of CHELSA V2.1, so it is a lower bound

**[Paleoclimate]{.paleo}: CHELSA-TRACE21**

- [Paleoclimate]{.paleo}: CHELSA-TRACE21 v1.0, the files downloaded on 31st December 2023 for VegVault 1.0.0, with `bio15` at age 0 downloaded again on 20th November 2026 (in VegVault 1.0.0 it was 0 south of 14.65° S because of a truncated download)
- Downloaded values for each 500-year time-slice between 0 and 18,000 years before present (BP)
- Selected bio-variables: `1`, `4`, `6`, `12`, `15`, `18`, `19`
- For each time slice, applied spatial aggregation using `terra::aggregate(factor = 25, fun = "median")`
- Inflated precipitation of the source in 25° S to 5° N and 80° W to 35° W, at 12,000, 12,500 and 15,000 to 18,000 years, masked: there, `bio12`, `bio15`, `bio18` and `bio19` have no value
- Precipitation stored in whole kg m^-2^, so a quarter with less than 0.5 kg m^-2^ is 0

**[HWSD Soil Data]{.abiotic}:**

- HWSD v2.2 downloaded on 20th November 2026 (both `hwsd2.2_raster.zip` and `hwsd2.2_db.zip`); VegVault 1.0.0 used HWSD v2.0 or v2.01, downloaded on 11th September 2023
- [Soil groups]{.abiotic}: the WRB 2022 Reference Soil Group of each cell, coded 1 to 32 in alphabetical order; a cell whose dominant class is not a soil (glaciers, open water) has no value
- The soil codes of VegVault 1.0.0 came from a wrong lookup and cannot be compared with those of v2.0.0
- [Resampled]{.reproducibility} using `terra::resample(method = "near")` function to match [climate data]{.abiotic} resolution
- Provides essential [edaphic context]{.abiotic} for vegetation-environment relationships ([contemporary data]{.neo-vegetation} only)

**Processing Details**: Available at [VegVault-abiotic_data](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24504826)

## Data Integration Procedures {.topic-database .topic-icon}

All [processing pipelines]{.reproducibility} with their corresponding [Tags]{.database} are migrated into an [SQLite database]{.database} using the GitHub repository titled [VegVault](https://github.com/OndrejMottl/VegVault/tree/v2.0.0), which can be accessed as DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.14777447](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14777447) (all versions).
The build is a `{targets}` pipeline in six stages: import of the pinned files, links between samples and gridpoints, assembly of the database, validation, export of the flat files, and the figures of the data paper.

### Data Migration Details {.topic-reproducibility}

**[Migrating sPlotOpen vegetation data]{.neo-vegetation}:**

- [Dataset name]{.database} (`dataset_name`) created from `plot_observation_id` as `splot_[plot_observation_id]`
- Original [data source]{.database} from column `givd_id` stored in `DatasetSourcesID` table
- [Sample name]{.database} (`sample_name`) created using `plot_observation_id` as `splot_[plot_observation_id]`
- [Sample Size]{.database} (`sample_size`) created from `releve_area` column
- All samples automatically assigned age of 0
- Taxonomic names extracted from `Species` column, abundances from `Original_abundance`; records without a species name are not stored

**Migrating BIEN vegetation data:**

- [Dataset name]{.database} (`dataset_name`) created from the plot identifier as `bien_[plot_id]` (VegVault 1.0.0 used the row number of the file, which changes when rows are added or reordered)
- Original [data source]{.database} from column `datasource` stored in `DatasetSourcesID` table
- [Sampling method]{.database} extracted from `methodology_description` column
- [Sample name]{.database} (`sample_name`) created as `bien_[plot_id]`
- [Sample Size]{.database} (`sample_size`) created from `plot_area_ha` column, multiplied by 10,000 (stored in square meters)
- All samples automatically assigned age of 0
- [Taxonomic names]{.taxa} extracted from `name_matched` column

**[Migrating fossil pollen data]{.paleo}:**

- [Dataset name]{.database} (`dataset_name`) created from the Neotoma dataset identifier as `fossilpol_[dataset_id]`
- Note: the Neotoma `dataset_id` in the name is not the `dataset_id` of the [VegVault]{.vegvault} table `Datasets`, which is numbered anew in every build
- Original [data source]{.database} from `source_of_data` column stored in `DatasetSourcesID` table
- [Sampling method]{.database} extracted from `depositionalenvironment` column
- Individual [Dataset Reference]{.database} extracted from `doi` column
- [Sample name]{.database} (`sample_name`) created from the Neotoma identifiers of the dataset and the sample as `fossilpol_[dataset_id]_[sample_id]` (VegVault 1.0.0 used the database identifier of the dataset here, so sample names changed with every build)
- [Ages]{.paleo} extracted from `levels` column
- [Age uncertainty]{.paleo} from age-depth models extracted from `age_uncertainty` column
- [Taxonomic names]{.taxa} and abundances extracted from `counts_harmonised` column; a taxon is stored for a sample only when its count is above zero

**[Migrating TRY functional traits]{.traits}:**

- [Dataset name]{.database} (`dataset_name`) created as `try_[number]`: one dataset per combination of data source, longitude, latitude and reference, numbered in the order of these values (VegVault 1.0.0 numbered them in the order of the file)
- Original [data source]{.database} from column `dataset` stored in `DatasetSourcesID` table
- Individual [Dataset Reference]{.database} extracted from `reference_source` column
- [Sample name]{.database} (`sample_name`) created from the TRY observation as `try_[observation_id]`
- Individual [Sample references]{.database} extracted from `dataset_reference_citation` and `record_reference` (the publication of each TRY record)
- All samples automatically assigned age of 0
- Trait names extracted from `trait_full_name`, taxonomic names from `acc_species_name`, trait values from `trait_value`, with their unit and conversion rule

**[Migrating BIEN functional traits]{.traits}:**

- [Dataset name]{.database} (`dataset_name`) created as `bien_traits_[number]`, by the same rule as for TRY
- Original [data source]{.database} from column `project_pi` stored in `DatasetSourcesID` table
- Individual [Dataset Reference]{.database} extracted from `source_citation` column
- [Sample name]{.database} (`sample_name`) created using column `id` as `bien_traits_[id]`
- All samples automatically assigned age of 0
- [Trait names]{.traits} extracted from `trait_full_name`, [taxonomic names]{.taxa} from `scrubbed_species_binomial`, [trait values]{.traits} from `trait_value`, with their unit and conversion rule

### Final Database Integration Procedures {.topic-reproducibility}

In addition to the consolidation of all [processed data]{.reproducibility} into a unified [SQLite database]{.database}, the final [VegVault]{.vegvault} migration repository performs three critical procedures to ensure [data consistency]{.reproducibility} and usability:

#### (i) Taxonomic Classification {.topic-taxa}

As [VegVault]{.vegvault} integrates data on [taxa]{.taxa} from various sources, the [{taxospace}]{.reproducibility} R package is used to classify diverse [taxa]{.taxa} into a unifying [taxonomic backbone]{.taxa}.
The [{taxospace}]{.reproducibility} tool automatically aligns [taxon names]{.taxa} with the [GBIF taxonomical backbone]{.taxa}.
Specifically, we find the best match of raw [taxon names]{.taxa} using the Global Names Verifier, which is then aligned with GBIF.
Only plant taxa count, each name is sent with only its first letter in capitals, and when a name matches several taxa equally well, the taxon with the smallest GBIF identifier is used.
The resulting [taxonomic classification]{.taxa} information, detailed up to the family level, is stored for each [taxon]{.taxa}, ensuring consistency and facilitating comparative analyses across different datasets.

Two kinds of names are corrected by hand after the automatic classification.
[Fossil pollen types]{.paleo} that combine two or more taxa (such as the Neotoma name "Betula/Carpinus", stored as "Betula Carpinus") keep only what their parts share: the family when all parts belong to one family, and no classification otherwise.
The pollen type "Pinus Picea" is classified as the family Pinaceae, the family of both genera, instead of *Abies alba*, to which the automatic matching resolves it.

**Important limitations**: [Taxonomic classification]{.taxa} down to the species level is not available for each [taxon]{.taxa} (e.g., some [fossil pollen types]{.paleo} can only be identified to the genus or family level).
For several [taxa]{.taxa}, no matching classification could be found.
Note that [taxonomic classification]{.taxa} is additional information—the original [taxon name]{.taxa} is always present and returned by default.
Finally, users should be aware that this classification is an [automated process]{.reproducibility} and may contain errors.

#### (ii) Grouping of Traits into Trait Domains {.topic-traits}

As there are differences in [trait names]{.traits} across data sources (e.g., "Leaf nitrogen (N) content per leaf dry mass" vs. "leaf nitrogen content per leaf dry mass"), we added a new variable `Trait Domain` that groups [traits]{.traits} together following the [trait selection]{.traits} of Díaz et al. (2016).
For example, [trait]{.traits} `Plant height vegetative` from [TRY]{.traits} and [trait]{.traits} `whole plant height` from [BIEN]{.traits} are both grouped under the [Trait Domain]{.traits} stored as `Plant heigh`, the spelling of VegVault 1.0.0.
This grouping serves as an efficient mechanism for extracting comparable [traits]{.traits} across both [TRY]{.traits} and [BIEN]{.traits} datasets.
Every [trait value]{.traits} is stored in the unit of its [Trait Domain]{.traits}, together with the rule that converted it.

#### (iii) Creation of Gridpoints for Abiotic Data {.topic-abiotic}

We developed a data structure that provides readily available [environmental context]{.abiotic} for each [vegetation]{.neo-vegetation} (and [trait]{.traits}) record by creating spatio-temporal links between these records and [abiotic information]{.abiotic}.
As raster data are not suitable for storage in an [SQLite database]{.database}, we created artificial points, called '[gridpoints]{.abiotic}', located in the center of each raster cell.
This resulted in a uniform spatio-temporal matrix of [gridpoints]{.abiotic} holding the [abiotic information]{.abiotic}.

**[Gridpoint naming conventions]{.reproducibility}**: `dataset_name` are created as "geo_[longitude]_[latitude]" and `sample_name` are created as "geo_[longitude]_[latitude]_[age]".

```{r}
#| label: link-limits
#| include: false

link_distance_km <-
  load_config_value(value = c("link", "distance_km"))

link_distance_years <-
  load_config_value(value = c("link", "distance_years"))
```

**[Spatial-temporal linking]{.reproducibility}**: We linked [gridpoints]{.abiotic} with every other non-gridpoint [Sample]{.database} (`vegetation_plot`, `fossil_pollen_archive`, and [traits]{.traits}) that lies at most `r link_distance_km` km and at most `r scales::label_comma()(link_distance_years)` years from it, and discarded the [gridpoint Samples]{.abiotic} without such a link.
The distance is the geodesic distance on the WGS84 ellipsoid; the distance and the age difference are stored truncated to whole kilometres and years.
Since v2.0.0 the rule is applied exactly: VegVault 1.0.0 searched only within one degree of longitude and did not wrap at the dateline, so it missed the links at high latitudes, where `r link_distance_km` km is more than one degree of longitude, and across the dateline.
The links are computed and stored once per position, a distinct combination of longitude, latitude and age (tables `Positions`, `SamplePosition` and `PositionLink`), and the view `AbioticDataReference` returns them per sample, as the table of the same name did in VegVault 1.0.0.
